---
title: "Data and modeling utilities"
output: html_notebook
---

Shared utilities for reading and validating data, encoding predictors,
fitting classifiers, generating predictions, and calculating weighted
performance metrics.

Defines functions for use by the numbered notebooks. Individual
notebooks control temporal splits, eligibility filtering, model selection,
and when these functions are executed.

## Input validation and transformations

These functions check the input schema and survey years, apply a consistent
predictor encoding, and distinguish missing predictors from unknown outcomes.

Recognized missing predictor responses are handled as explicit categories.
Invalid or unknown outcomes remain "missing" and individual notebooks will
exclude those outcomes from supervised model fitting, as needed.

```{r input-validation-and-transformations}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Package dependencies
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Check that required packages are installed. Stops and alerts.
check_packages <- function(
    packages = c("data.table", "ggplot2", "glmnet", "ranger", "Matrix")
) {
    missing <- packages[
        !vapply(packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
    ]

    if (length(missing)) {
        stop(
            "Missing R packages: ",
            paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
            ". Run notebooks/00_Install_Packages.Rmd first."
        )
    }

    invisible(TRUE)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Input readers and schema validation
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Reads data file (RDS) and verifies fields and years expected by the workflow
# are present.
read_input <- function(path, years) {
    if (!file.exists(path)) {
        stop("Required input file is missing: ", path)
    }

    data <- data.table::as.data.table(readRDS(path))

    # Addresses inheritance, individual year input inherits year from function.
    # Multi-year inputs must already identify the year of each record.
    if (!"YEAR" %in% names(data) && length(years) == 1L) {
        data[, YEAR := years]
    }

    required <- c(
        "YEAR",
        "STATE",
        "STRAT",
        "PSU",
        "RAW_WEIGHT",
        "FMD",
        "AIAN_ALONE",
        "PHYSHLTH_DAYS",
        "GENHLTH_CLEAN",
        "AGE_BAND",
        "SEX_CLEAN",
        "EDU_CLEAN",
        "INCOME_BAND"
    )

    missing <- setdiff(required, names(data))

    if (length(missing)) {
        stop(
            "Missing input columns: ",
            paste(missing, collapse = ", ")
        )
    }

    # Confirms the expected set of years.
    if (!setequal(unique(data$YEAR), years)) {
        stop("Unexpected survey years in ", basename(path))
    }

    # Preserves record's position within this input file for traceability.
    # This identifier is local to the file.
    data[, source_row_id := seq_len(.N)]

    data
}


# Load the historical file and require all years from 2014 through 2024.
read_historical <- function() {
    read_input(data_historical, 2014:2024)
}


# Load the held-out test file and confirm the 2025 survey year.
read_test_year <- function() {
    read_input(data_test, 2025L)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validity checks and evaluation groups
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Accept only finite, positive survey and training weights.
valid_weight <- function(weights) {
    is.finite(weights) & weights > 0
}


# Accept only observed binary outcomes coded as 0 or 1.
valid_outcome <- function(outcome) {
    !is.na(outcome) & outcome %in% c(0, 1)
}


# Translate supplied AI/AN-alone indicator into evaluation-group labels.
# The meaning of FALSE depends on the indicator's upstream coding.
# Missing or otherwise unmatched values retain the unresolved label.
race_group <- function(indicator) {
    result <- rep("Unresolved/multiracial", length(indicator))

    result[!is.na(indicator) & indicator == TRUE] <- primary_groups[1]
    result[!is.na(indicator) & indicator == FALSE] <- primary_groups[2]

    result
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Categorical encoding
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Standardize non-response to an explicit "Missing" category.
# Reject unexpected labels rather than silently creating new categories.
strict_factor <- function(value, allowed_levels, variable) {
    label <- trimws(as.character(value))

    not_answered <- is.na(value) | label %in% c(
        "",
        "NA",
        "NaN",
        "Unknown",
        "Refused",
        "Don't know",
        "Don't know/Not sure",
        "Missing"
    )

    label[not_answered] <- "Missing"

    unexpected <- setdiff(unique(label), allowed_levels)

    if (length(unexpected)) {
        stop(
            variable,
            " has unexpected levels: ",
            paste(unexpected, collapse = ", ")
        )
    }

    # Use the configured levels and ordering even when some categories
    # are absent from the current subset.
    factor(label, levels = allowed_levels)
}


# Prepares predictors, evaluation groups, and the labeled classification target.
# Works on a copy so data.table assignments do not modify the data.
prepare_features <- function(data) {
    data <- data.table::copy(data.table::as.data.table(data))

    # Convert physical-health days to numeric before checking their range.
    physical_days <- suppressWarnings(
        as.numeric(as.character(data$PHYSHLTH_DAYS))
    )

    # Observed numeric values must be whole numbers between 0 and 30.
    invalid_days <- !is.na(physical_days) & (
        physical_days < 0 |
        physical_days > 30 |
        physical_days != floor(physical_days)
    )
    # Any unexpected values indicate a problem with the annual recoding.
    if (any(invalid_days)) {
        stop("Unexpected physical-health day codes; inspect annual recoding")
    }

    # Map valid day counts into five configured intervals.
    # Half-day boundaries separate the integer-valued categories.
    physical_label <- cut(
        physical_days,
        breaks = c(-0.5, 0.5, 6.5, 13.5, 20.5, 30.5),
        labels = factor_levels$physical_days_group[1:5],
        include.lowest = TRUE
    )

    data[, physical_days_group := strict_factor(
        physical_label,
        factor_levels$physical_days_group,
        "PHYSHLTH_DAYS"
    )]

    data[, general_health_group := strict_factor(
        GENHLTH_CLEAN,
        factor_levels$general_health_group,
        "GENHLTH_CLEAN"
    )]

    # Applies categorical schema to the remaining predictors.
    for (variable in c("AGE_BAND", "SEX_CLEAN", "EDU_CLEAN", "INCOME_BAND")) {
        data.table::set(
            data,
            j = variable,
            value = strict_factor(
                data[[variable]],
                factor_levels[[variable]],
                variable
            )
        )
    }

    # Maintains evaluation-group membership separate from the model predictors.
    data[, cohort := race_group(AIAN_ALONE)]

    # Labels valid outcomes for classification without changing the FMD column.
    # Unknown or invalid outcomes remain NA.
    outcome_labels <- ifelse(
        valid_outcome(data$FMD),
        ifelse(data$FMD == 1, "Yes", "No"),
        NA_character_
    )

    data[, outcome_factor := factor(
        outcome_labels,
        levels = c("No", "Yes")
    )]

    # Missing responses explicit predictor categories.
    # Any remaining NA indicates an encoding problem.
    if (anyNA(data[, ..feature_names])) {
        stop("Feature encoding left missing predictor values")
    }

    data
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Weight utilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Calculate weighted mean using finite values and valid weights.
# Return NA when there are no usable observations.
weighted_mean <- function(value, weights) {
    keep <- is.finite(value) & valid_weight(weights)

    if (!any(keep)) {
        return(NA_real_)
    }

    sum(value[keep] * weights[keep]) / sum(weights[keep])
}


# Rescales training weights to have a mean of one.
# Relative weights preserved while their scale is standardized.
normalize_weights <- function(weights) {
    if (any(!valid_weight(weights))) {
        stop("Model training requires finite positive weights")
    }

    weights / mean(weights)
}
```

## Model training and metrics

These functions use the configured predictor schema to fit and evaluate
classifiers for frequent mental distress.

Individual notebooks supply appropriate training years and valid
supervised outcomes. Computational subsampling is accounted for through
inverse-probability adjustments to the training weights.

The performance functions calculate weighted point estimates.

```{r model-training-and-metrics}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Development-sample construction
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Retain all AI/AN-alone records and sample the other groups within each year.
sample_development <- function(data) {
    data <- data.table::copy(data.table::as.data.table(data))

    data[, sampling_group := race_group(AIAN_ALONE)]

    groups <- unique(data$sampling_group)
    collected <- list()
    index <- 0L

    for (group in groups) {
        subset <- data[sampling_group == group]

        # Keep the entire primary group; use configured targets for others.
        cap <- if (group == primary_groups[1]) {
            nrow(subset)
        } else if (group == primary_groups[2]) {
            comparison_cap
        } else {
            unknown_cap
        }

        count <- nrow(subset)

        if (count == 0L) {
            next
        }

        years <- sort(unique(subset$YEAR))

        for (year in years) {
            annual <- subset[YEAR == year]

            # Allocate the group-level target in proportion to annual counts.
            # Retain at least one record from each represented year.
            # Rounding means the total is not necessarily an exact hard cap.
            if (count <= cap) {
                number <- nrow(annual)
            } else {
                number <- min(
                    nrow(annual),
                    max(
                        1L,
                        as.integer(
                            round(as.numeric(cap) * nrow(annual) / count)
                        )
                    )
                )
            }

            # Avoid random sampling when every annual record is retained.
            # Otherwise, sample without replacement within this group-year.
            choice <- if (number == nrow(annual)) {
                seq_len(number)
            } else {
                sample.int(
                    nrow(annual),
                    size = number,
                    replace = FALSE
                )
            }

            sampled <- annual[choice]

            # Record the computational sampling probability so retained
            # records can represent the observations not selected.
            sampled[, inclusion_probability := number / nrow(annual)]

            index <- index + 1L
            collected[[index]] <- sampled
        }
    }

    sampled <- data.table::rbindlist(collected, use.names = TRUE)

    # Combine the original survey weight with the subsampling adjustment.
    sampled[, train_weight := RAW_WEIGHT / inclusion_probability]

    if (any(!valid_weight(sampled$train_weight))) {
        stop("Invalid inverse-probability training weight")
    }

    # Remove the temporary grouping field; retain sampling metadata.
    sampled[, sampling_group := NULL]

    sampled
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Design-matrix construction
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Build a sparse predictor matrix using the shared feature list.
# Consistent factor levels help keep the encoding aligned across data subsets.
matrix_inputs <- function(data) {
    formula <- stats::reformulate(feature_names)

    matrix <- Matrix::sparse.model.matrix(
        formula,
        data = as.data.frame(data)
    )

    # Remove the formula-generated intercept column.
    # glmnet handles its own intercept by default.
    matrix[, colnames(matrix) != "(Intercept)", drop = FALSE]
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Classifier fitting
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Fit one supported classifier using the supplied training records.
# "parameter" represents lambda for lasso or mtry for the random forest.
# It is unused for ordinary logistic regression.
fit_classifier <- function(family, training, parameter = NA_real_) {
    training <- as.data.frame(training)
    weights <- normalize_weights(training$train_weight)

    if (family == "logistic") {
        # Store weights in the model data so formula evaluation can find them.
        training$.model_weight <- weights

        formula <- stats::reformulate(
            feature_names,
            response = "FMD"
        )

        # Warnings are suppressed in the existing workflow.
        # Convergence is checked explicitly after fitting.
        model <- suppressWarnings(
            stats::glm(
                formula,
                data = training,
                family = stats::binomial(),
                weights = .model_weight,
                control = stats::glm.control(maxit = 60)
            )
        )

        if (!isTRUE(model$converged)) {
            stop("Weighted logistic regression did not converge")
        }

        return(list(
            family = family,
            model = model
        ))
    }

    if (family == "lasso") {
        # Fit penalized logistic regression at the supplied penalty value.
        # alpha = 1 selects the lasso penalty.
        model <- glmnet::glmnet(
            x = matrix_inputs(training),
            y = training$FMD,
            family = "binomial",
            alpha = 1,
            lambda = as.numeric(parameter),
            weights = weights,
            standardize = TRUE,
            maxit = 100000
        )

        return(list(
            family = family,
            model = model,
            lambda = as.numeric(parameter)
        ))
    }

    if (family == "forest") {
        # Supply only the configured predictors and labeled outcome.
        forest_data <- training[
            ,
            c(feature_names, "outcome_factor"),
            drop = FALSE
        ]

        formula <- stats::reformulate(
            feature_names,
            response = "outcome_factor"
        )

        # Fit a probability forest and retain permutation importance.
        # Bound mtry by the number of available predictors.
        model <- ranger::ranger(
            formula,
            data = forest_data,
            probability = TRUE,
            case.weights = weights,
            num.trees = forest_trees,
            mtry = min(as.integer(parameter), length(feature_names)),
            min.node.size = 40,
            importance = "permutation",
            num.threads = rf_threads,
            seed = seed
        )

        return(list(
            family = family,
            model = model,
            mtry = as.integer(parameter)
        ))
    }

    stop("Unsupported model family: ", family)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Probability prediction
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Provide one prediction interface across the supported model families.
# Each branch returns the estimated probability of the positive outcome.
predict_classifier <- function(fitted, data) {
    data <- as.data.frame(data)

    if (fitted$family == "logistic") {
        # glm drops factor levels absent from its training years, so predict()
        # fails when a later year first contains one (e.g. SEX_CLEAN "Missing").
        # Build the design matrix from the full factor schema instead; a level
        # the model never saw has no coefficient and contributes zero, as in the
        # lasso fit. Identical to predict.glm whenever every level was seen.
        coefficients <- stats::coef(fitted$model)
        coefficients[is.na(coefficients)] <- 0
        design <- stats::model.matrix(
            stats::reformulate(feature_names),
            data = data
        )
        stopifnot(all(names(coefficients) %in% colnames(design)))
        prediction <- as.numeric(
            stats::plogis(
                design[, names(coefficients), drop = FALSE] %*% coefficients
            )
        )
    } else if (fitted$family == "lasso") {
        prediction <- as.numeric(
            stats::predict(
                fitted$model,
                newx = matrix_inputs(data),
                s = fitted$lambda,
                type = "response"
            )
        )
    } else if (fitted$family == "forest") {
        prediction <- predict(
            fitted$model,
            data = data[, feature_names, drop = FALSE],
            num.threads = rf_threads
        )$predictions[, "Yes"]
    } else {
        stop("Cannot predict with unknown model family")
    }

    # Require one finite prediction per input record.
    if (
        length(prediction) != nrow(data) ||
        any(!is.finite(prediction))
    ) {
        stop("Model predictions have invalid size or probabilities")
    }

    # Return a numeric vector bounded to the probability interval.
    pmin(1, pmax(0, as.numeric(prediction)))
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Weighted discrimination: area under the ROC curve
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Calculate AUC from weighted positive-negative comparisons.
# Equal prediction scores receive half credit.
weighted_auc <- function(y, p, w) {
    valid <- valid_outcome(y) & is.finite(p) & valid_weight(w)

    y <- y[valid]
    p <- p[valid]
    w <- w[valid]

    # Discrimination is undefined when either outcome class is absent.
    if (!any(y == 0) || !any(y == 1)) {
        return(NA_real_)
    }

    ranked <- data.table::data.table(
        score = p,
        positive = w * (y == 1),
        negative = w * (y == 0)
    )

    # Aggregate tied scores before accumulating negative-class weight.
    ranked <- ranked[
        ,
        .(
            pos = sum(positive),
            neg = sum(negative)
        ),
        by = score
    ][order(score)]

    negative_below <- c(
        0,
        head(cumsum(ranked$neg), -1)
    )

    # Count lower-scoring negatives plus half of tied negative weight.
    sum(ranked$pos * (negative_below + 0.5 * ranked$neg)) /
        (sum(ranked$pos) * sum(ranked$neg))
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Weighted performance summary
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Summarize valid outcomes, probabilities, and survey weights.
# Invalid records are excluded from every metric in this summary.
weighted_metrics <- function(y, p, w) {
    valid <- (
        valid_outcome(y) &
        is.finite(p) &
        p >= 0 &
        p <= 1 &
        valid_weight(w)
    )

    y <- y[valid]
    p <- p[valid]
    w <- w[valid]

    if (!length(y)) {
        stop("No valid classified records for metric calculation")
    }

    observed <- weighted_mean(y, w)
    predicted <- weighted_mean(p, w)

    data.frame(
        # Unweighted number of records contributing to the metrics.
        n = length(y),

        # Weight-based effective sample size; not a full survey-design ESS.
        effective_n = sum(w)^2 / sum(w^2),

        # Compare weighted outcome prevalence with mean predicted probability.
        prevalence = observed,
        mean_prediction = predicted,

        # Positive values indicate average overprediction.
        # This is a signed mean difference, not a full calibration assessment.
        calibration_error = predicted - observed,

        # Summarize discrimination and squared probability error.
        auc = weighted_auc(y, p, w),
        brier = weighted_mean((y - p)^2, w)
    )
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Weighted ROC-curve coordinates
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Build ROC coordinates by lowering the threshold through distinct scores.
# Reduce the returned points for display after calculating the cumulative curve.
weighted_roc <- function(y, p, w, display_points = 300L) {
    valid <- valid_outcome(y) & is.finite(p) & valid_weight(w)

    ranked <- data.table::data.table(
        score = p[valid],
        positive = w[valid] * (y[valid] == 1),
        negative = w[valid] * (y[valid] == 0)
    )

    # Process tied scores together, starting with the highest predictions.
    ranked <- ranked[
        ,
        .(
            pos = sum(positive),
            neg = sum(negative)
        ),
        by = score
    ][order(-score)]

    # Both outcome classes are required to define the ROC curve.
    if (!sum(ranked$pos) || !sum(ranked$neg)) {
        return(data.frame(
            fpr = NA_real_,
            tpr = NA_real_
        ))
    }

    # Include the initial point where no records are classified as positive.
    fpr <- c(0, cumsum(ranked$neg) / sum(ranked$neg))
    tpr <- c(0, cumsum(ranked$pos) / sum(ranked$pos))

    # Select approximately evenly spaced positions along the coordinate list.
    indices <- unique(
        as.integer(
            round(
                seq(
                    1,
                    length(fpr),
                    length.out = min(display_points, length(fpr))
                )
            )
        )
    )

    data.frame(
        fpr = fpr[indices],
        tpr = tpr[indices]
    )
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Probability recalibration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Apply an already-estimated calibration intercept and slope.
# This function transforms predictions; it does not estimate the parameters.
calibrate_probabilities <- function(p, intercept, slope) {
    # Clip exact zero and one before converting probabilities to log-odds.
    linear_score <- stats::qlogis(
        pmin(1 - 1e-6, pmax(1e-6, p))
    )

    # Adjust the log-odds, then convert back to probabilities.
    stats::plogis(intercept + slope * linear_score)
}
```
